_note: Hand-written patterns in my own words. Weight = how suspicious (1 low .. 4 high). Keywords are matched case-insensitively as whole words/phrases. Extend or adjust as needed.

patterns.name: Urgency / account lock threat
patterns.explanation: Creates panic so you act before thinking.

patterns.name: Asks for OTP / TAC / password
patterns.explanation: Real banks never ask you to share OTP/TAC or passwords by message or call.

patterns.name: Prize / lucky draw claim
patterns.explanation: Unexpected prizes are a classic bait to collect fees or personal data.

patterns.name: Parcel / delivery fee
patterns.explanation: Fake courier notices ask for a small fee through a link.

patterns.name: Tax / refund claim
patterns.explanation: Fake refund messages try to collect bank details.

patterns.name: Pressure to pay or transfer
patterns.explanation: Direct requests to pay or transfer money are a strong warning sign.

patterns.name: Impersonating police / court / central bank
patterns.explanation: Macau-scam style: fake officials claim you are in trouble.

patterns.name: Job / easy-money offer
patterns.explanation: Unrealistic pay for simple tasks, often followed by deposits.

patterns.name: Investment with guaranteed returns
patterns.explanation: No legitimate investment can guarantee returns.

patterns.name: Romance / emergency money request
patterns.explanation: Fake relationships build trust, then ask for money.

patterns.name: Secrecy request
patterns.explanation: Scammers isolate victims so nobody can warn them.

patterns.name: Threat of penalty / freezing
patterns.explanation: Fear of consequences is used to rush decisions.

patterns.name: Install app / remote access
patterns.explanation: Malicious apps or remote tools let scammers control your phone.

patterns.name: Click-this-link instruction
patterns.explanation: On its own common, but suspicious combined with other signals.

patterns.name: E-wallet verification
patterns.explanation: Fake e-wallet upgrade/verification notices steal logins.

patterns.name: Utility cut-off threat
patterns.explanation: Fake utility notices threaten disconnection unless you pay.

patterns.name: Bank brand mentioned
patterns.explanation: Brand names are used to look official. Check the sender and link domain.

patterns.name: Wrong-number opener
patterns.explanation: A harmless-looking opener used to start a conversation with a target.
